input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
input.rationale: Clause 28.1 selects Singapore law with exclusive Singapore jurisdiction — Vendor-side foreign law and venue outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), i.e. walk-away territory, and it directly conflicts with 28.2, which already confers exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County with only a customary temporary injunctive relief carve-out (which does not defeat the exclusive merits forum). The shortest cure is to switch the governing law in 28.1 to New York and delete the conflicting Singapore forum words, leaving 28.2 untouched so the preferred position is met in full.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
mappings.quote: The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.

proposal.summary: Replace Singapore governing law and exclusive Singapore venue in 28.1 with New York law, leaving 28.2's New York County exclusive jurisdiction intact.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced Singapore law and exclusive Singapore venue with New York law, which is our accepted position and removes the direct conflict with 28.2's exclusive New York County jurisdiction. Delaware, California, or England and Wales law with the corresponding courts would be an acceptable fallback.
